name: Pieter — 130 thermic hours at one big site, never flown cross-country
summary: Thirteen years of flying the same mountain site, well past 100 hours of thermic time, practises asymmetrics and spirals regularly, excellent judgement and decision-making, honest about his near misses. Has never flown another site and has never left the hill on a cross-country. Ground handling is basic, he only uses the bar to escape sink, and nobody qualified has watched him fly in years.
why_this_persona: The test of how the two new questions behave. Site variety and cross-country experience are scored properly at this step for the first time, and the design decision is that they can tip a borderline pilot a band but can never block a strong one. Pieter is the borderline pilot: his site-variety and cross-country answers together cost him around five points of skills, which — stacked on basic kiting, no bar use and nobody having seen him fly — pulls his skills below the Ready floor while his near-perfect judgement keeps his total in the Ready band. The result is Nearly ready with the skills category floor named, which is the honest answer. A scorer that gates him on either new question has made a pilot-rating requirement into a wing-class gate, which knowledge/disagreements.md point 5 forbids.

notes: Computed skills 65.1, psychological 100.0, total 81.5, no bonus. His total clears the Ready threshold of 78 but his skills score is well under the 72 category floor, so the two halves are doing visibly different things — which is what the category floors exist to catch, and the only persona in this set that exercises 'ready_category_floor:skills'.

NO GATE fires, and that is the central assertion. In particular neither new question gates: 'home site only' and 'no cross-country yet' cost him roughly five points of skills between them and nothing else. knowledge/steps/high-b-to-low-c.md's own caveat is that the USHPA P4 and BHPA Advanced Pilot figures are "supporting, non-gating signals at this step", and knowledge/disagreements.md point 14 adds Joy Paragliding arguing against tying wing upgrades to kilometres at all.

He also passes every critical_check_floor member, including the two that sit exactly on the 0.5 line ('never had a collapse' and 'I know where the reserve handle is'). Neither new question is a member of that list, deliberately — a Ready-block is a soft gate, and gating on pilot-rating criteria by another name is what the design decision declined to do.

'local_plans_and_this_wings_purpose' must NOT fire. He ticks local_soaring, which is half the local_only profile, but he also ticks first_xc — and the profile requires NO cross-country ambition. He isn't a local-only pilot; he's a pilot who has only flown locally so far and wants that to change, which is a different thing and gets different advice.

'build_thermic_hours' must NOT fire: he is past 100 thermic hours, which is the top of the published range. His gap is breadth, not hours — and showing him an hours suggestion would be the clearest possible sign that the rubric had confused the two.
'siv_before_you_upgrade' fires on 'never had a collapse' and on not having done a course, even though he practises regularly. That breadth is intended at this step.

TONE CHECK: his judgement and decision-making are perfect and his hours are there. The result has to read as 'go and fly somewhere else, and go further' — a to-do list that happens to be enjoyable — not as a verdict on thirteen years of flying one hill.
